thread:
Noah: Quick eyeball on dark-theme PR. Two quick pain points: (1) line markers in small charts barely read against the charcoal panel, (2) the new 'spectral' heatmap looks muddy at low values. Posting Figma frame: https://www.figma.com/file/zzz/dark-theming-experiments (frame 'Metrics + Code - Dark').

Riya: Can you include which components? is it the mini-sparkline or the big dashboard charts?

Noah: Mini-sparklines (12px markers) and the token-frequency heatmap. Markers use '--chart-marker: #ffd27a' currently, heatmap is the new spectral ramp.

Kofi: Small markers need higher contrast; at 12px they behave like hairlines. Suggest either 1) darker amber '#e6a85a' or 2) add a 1px halo ring (outline) in rgba(0,0,0,0.35) to separate from bg. Halo keeps hue but increases legibility.

Elaine: For the heatmap, 'spectral' ramps (rainbow-like) are perceptually non-monotonic and confuse density interpretation. Strong vote for a single-hue sequential ramp (dark->bright) or a perceptually-uniform viridis/plasma family. PaletteBot can run a quick check.

PaletteBot: Accessibility scan: '--chart-marker #ffd27a' on panel #0f1720 = 3.9:1 (borderline). heatmap spectral midpoint '#c83bff' on bg #0b0f13 = 2.1:1 (FAIL). Recommendation: sequential ramp based on hue=140 (greens) or viridis-like ['#053061','#2166ac','#4393c3','#92c5de','#f7f7f7'] (example) OR use multi-hue but ensure luminance monotonicity.

Riya: I like monotonic luminance. For token heatmap we need clear steps at low density (5-25%). Proposed sequential greens: ['#041a0f','#083c22','#0e6440','#16a46a','#6fe2a9']. Keeps green brand vibes but readable. I'll add Figma swatches.

Noah: On the marker halo idea, implementation-wise we can CSS-layer with an SVG stroke: `circle { stroke: rgba(0,0,0,0.36); stroke-width: 1.2; }` Works for canvas/SVG charts. Any perf concerns?

Kofi: SVG stroke is cheap. For canvas we can draw shadow first. Both fine. But prefer token change + halo only for micro charts to avoid visual clutter on large charts. We'll conditionally apply via CSS token `--marker-halo: 1 | 0`.

Elaine: Also a copy/accessibility nit: toggle label currently 'Dark' which is ambiguous in some languages. Suggest 'Enable dark theme' with aria-label='Toggle site theme: enable dark theme' so screen-readers read intent. Persist preference in account settings and localStorage fallback.

Noah: Agree. Also raise the question: naming convention for tokens. We're mixing `--chart-marker` and `--marker-halo` with `--heatmap-mid`. Can we standardize to `--chart-*` family for all visualization tokens? e.g., `--chart-marker`, `--chart-marker-halo`, `--chart-heatmap-0`..`-4`.

Riya: Good call. I'll rename tokens in Figma and create a migration note for FE. Avoid breaking themes that read old tokens.

PaletteBot: Contrast audit for proposed marker color '#e6a85a' on panel #0f1720 = 4.6:1 (PASS). Sequential-green midpoint '#0e6440' on bg #0b0f13 = 3.9:1 (borderline for small text but heatmap uses filled cells so ok). Viridis last step '#fde725' on bg = 6.8:1 (high but maybe too bright visually). Consider toning last stop down slightly.

Kofi: For charts with lines + markers, ensure stroke widths adapt in dark theme: `--chart-line-width: 2` for dark to improve visibility. We'll increase default for any line under 16px height.

Elaine: Keyboard focus: when user tabs into a chart legend pill, focus ring is subtle. Use `outline: 3px solid rgba(94,160,255,0.18)` and ensure it doesn't clip inside rounded corners. Also add `:focus-visible` polyfill for Safari.

Noah: Plan: @Riya update Figma swatches + token rename; @Kofi add halo + line-width conditional in chart component; @Elaine update i18n copy + focus styles; I'll run a staging check once PRs land and re-run PaletteBot. :thumbsup:

Riya: I'll push Figma changes and a token map before EOD.

Kofi: I'll feature-flag the halo and extra width behind `chartsDarkAccessibility` flag. Will include visual regression screenshots.

Elaine: I'll update the copy and add accessibility notes to the PR template.

PaletteBot: Requested re-scan when tokens renamed. Good discussion. :sparkles:
